papers.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
papers.abstract: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.

papers.title: Noncommutative weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity over locally compact quantum groups
papers.abstract: We study weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity for Hopf-von Neumann algebras and locally compact quantum groups. For a Hopf-von Neumann algebra $(M,\Gamma)$, we introduce the space ${\rm WAP}_{{\rm Bessel},\pi_u}(M_*)$ through norm convergence conditions on rows and columns of slices associated with Bessel families in the universal representation. We prove that this space is the largest $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm WAP}(M_*)$ when separately continuous lift of the co-multiplication is multiplicative, and that the two spaces coincide when $M$ is commutative. Furthermore, the algebra $\{x\in C_b(\mathbb{G}): \Gamma(x)\in M(C_0(\mathbb{G})\otimes C_b(\mathbb{G}))\}$ is characterized as the greatest left introverted $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ satisfying a left Bessel condition on $L^2(\mathbb{G})$. We also show that ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ is a $C^*$-algebra whenever the center of $C_0(\mathbb{G})$ contains an element on which the bounded counit is non-zero.

papers.title: Algebras, Kernels and Correspondences
papers.abstract: This is a nearly complete draft of our paper in which we attempt to do three things. First, we show that when formulated in the context of reproducing kernel correspondences over Rieffel's category, Normod-$M$, the Kolmogorov decomposition/representation theorem of Ball, Marx, and Vinnikov is functorial in $M$. Second, we investigate relations between our work and the work of Clou\^atre and Hartz concerning multipliers of reproducing kernels. This investigation leads to interesting questions about the geometry of the matricial unit disc associated with a correspondence over $M$. And third, we describe how some of the recent work of Salomon, Shalit and Shamovich may be formulated in our setting. This leads to the notion of subvarieties, their quotients, and their relation with the structure of reproducing correspondences.

papers.title: Functional relations for higher-order free cumulants
papers.abstract: We establish the functional relations between generating series of higher-order free cumulants and moments in higher-order free probability, solving an open problem posed fifteen years ago by Collins, Mingo, \'Sniady and Speicher. We propose an extension of free probability theory, which governs the all-order topological expansion in unitarily invariant matrix ensembles, with a corresponding notion of free cumulants and give as well their relation to moments via functional relations. Our approach is based on the study of a master transformation involving double monotone Hurwitz numbers via semi-infinite wedge techniques, building on the recent advances of the last-named author with Bychkov, Dunin-Barkowski and Kazarian. We illustrate our formulas by computing the first few decaying terms of the correlation functions of an ensemble of spiked GUE matrices, going beyond the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem.

papers.title: Pointwise convergence of noncommutative discrete spherical ergodic averages
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish spherical maximal inequalities associated with commuting trace-preserving automorphisms on von Neumann algebras, extending Magyar-Stein-Wainger's discrete spherical maximal inequalities to the noncommutative setting. On a noncommutative probability space, we further prove that, under a strong ergodicity assumption, the corresponding discrete spherical averages converge bilaterally almost uniformly to $\tau(x)1$ for every $x\in L_p(\mathcal M)$, $\frac{d}{d-2}<p\leq\infty$, when $d\geq5$.

papers.title: Dynamics in large scale geometry
papers.abstract: We investigate the large scale geometry of certain metric spaces through the lens of dynamics. Our approach establishes a close connection between large scale dynamical phenomena and operator algebras by characterizing various large scale dynamic behaviors in terms of GNS representations of the uniform Roe algebras arising from natural canonical states. Our dynamical systems are given by the Stone-\v{C}ech boundary of metric spaces together with their inverse semigroup of partial translations. This defines a space of orbits and we characterize Hausdorffness and $T_1$-ness of this space by the failure of coarse embeddability of certain metric spaces. Surprisingly, while the orbit space has very weak separation properties, we show that it satisfies a certain ''localized version'' of Urysohn's lemma. We show that the topology of the space of orbits and quasi-orbits are given by the space of irreducible representations of uniform Roe algebras and by the space of their primitive ideals, respectively. As a highlight of the theory developed herein, we provide classes of spaces such that the prime ideals of their uniform Roe algebras are primitive. This is the case for instance of spaces whose orbit space is $T_1$.

papers.title: Values of Rokhlin Dimension for Integer Actions
papers.abstract: For an action of the integers on a C*-algebra, we show that the only possible values for the Rokhlin dimension (with commuting towers) are $0,1,2$ and $+\infty$. We study these values for certain classes of C*-algebras, and show that there is an automorphism of the Jiang--Su algebra with the property that its Rokhlin dimension with and without commuting towers are distinct.

papers.title: A characterization of purely atomic von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal semifinite trace $\tau$, and let $\Phi$ be an Orlicz function. We prove that the noncommutative Orlicz space $L^\Phi(M,\tau)$ is contained in $M$ if and only if $M$ is purely atomic and there is $\delta>0$ such that $\tau(e)\geq\delta$ for every nonzero projection $e\in M$. We also prove that every left $M$-module map on $L^\Phi(M,\tau)$ is bounded. As a consequence, a left ideal of $M$ contained in $L^\Phi(M,\tau)$ and dense in it admits an $M$-invariant algebraic complement if and only if it is equal to $L^\Phi(M,\tau)$. These results extend a theorem of Fidaleo and Zsid\'o from $L^2$ to all noncommutative Orlicz spaces.

papers.title: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem in operator algebras
papers.abstract: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem up to similarity in operator algebras asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$. We construct block-diagonal compact operators for which this implication fails. For von Neumann algebras with separable predual, we prove that this cancellation property is equivalent to subhomogeneity. Moreover, we obtain a cancellation law for finite ampliations in unital Banach algebras when the commutant of one element is finite dimensional modulo its Jacobson radical.
